title: Field Spark — Ops Innovation Kit (sketch)
body:
Goal: rapid, lightweight seller + ops materials to launch 2-week pilots with platform teams. Not a polished deck — this is the working sketch for SEs and Ops to iterate from.

Audience:
- SEs running pilot conversations with platform/integration engineers (mid-market + enterprise).
- Field ops who may be asked to run a live canary or validate fallbacks.

One-line value to lead with:
- "Redwood keeps your critical inference paths up while lowering per-token costs — here are pragmatic ways to prove it in 2 weeks."

Quick narrative (3 slides / 90s):
1) Why this matters: unpredictable token cost + latency spikes are the #1 blocker for product rollouts. Show a single graph: request rate vs tail-latency with/without prefix-KV cache. (placeholder: show sample numbers: 95th latency 420ms -> 160ms with caching + batching).
2) How Redwood helps: unified runtime + routing + fallback tiers -> predictable SLOs + cost levers. Bullet out: dedicated capacity option, private VPC, automatic prefix caching, quantization recommendation engine.
3) Pilot ask + success criteria: 2-week integration, sample 5000-chat-turns, measure cost per 1k tokens, 95th latency, and user-perceived error rate (semantic regressions).

Quick scripts (SE friendly) — 30–60s lines:
- Opener for platform engineer: "We can run a scoped integration for 2 weeks with no code changes to your client — we’ll route requests to a safe model variant and measure real traffic economics. If latency or quality looks off, we fall back automatically and capture traces so we can iterate."
- Cost question deflection: "We target cost predictability — we’ll show you a per-route estimate and a simulated monthly spend at three traffic levels within 48 hours."
- Security question: "Private control plane + optional VPC/on-prem deployment; all keys stay in your KMS when required."

Objection-swaps (rapid):
- "Model drift is scary": show eval harness + regression alerts tied to seed prompts; propose a canary sample set and rollback policy.
- "We can’t rely on hosted endpoints": propose Redwood Dedicated proof of concept (reserved pool) or Private small-hosted node in your VPC for the pilot.
- "Latency": show optimized kernel & batching explanation + offer a latency sim with their 99th percentile request size.

Pilot-contract checklist (tactical steps for SE / Ops):
- Pre-pilot sync: collect sample traffic profile, SLO targets, compliance checklist (SOC / KMS). Create JIRA ticket JIRA-4821 (owner: SE).
- Kickoff (day 0): route traffic to canary endpoint, enable tracing, set alerts for >2x expected latency.
- Week 1: run A/B (live): 50/50 traffic routing; collect token-level cost & top-10 prompt patterns.
- Week 2: enable caching, adjust batching sizes, test fallback to smaller quantized model.
- Exit: deliver 3 metrics: cost per 1k tokens, 95th latency, and semantic pass rate on sample prompts. Decision options: move to Dedicated reserve discussion / continue pilot / stop.

Ops runbook snippets (copyable):
- Canary endpoint config:
  - model: redwood/curated-medium-v2 (placeholder)
  - routing policy: primary-hosted -> dedicated -> small-quantized fallback
  - batching target: 64 tokens / batch (adjust for median request length)
  - KV cache: prefix enabled for repeated request patterns

- Alert thresholds (example):
  - 95th latency > 500ms for 5m window -> page on-call SRE
  - Token cost per minute > projected by 30% -> notify account lead + SE
  - Quality regression > 5% on seed set -> pause rollout + notify product/ML

Quick technical diagrams (text placeholders):
- Diagram A: client -> load-balancer -> routing policy -> [hosted pool | dedicated pool | private node] -> model variants.
- Diagram B: request flow illustrating KV cache hit and short-circuit to host with cached KV.

Field play snippets (to include in slide deck):
- "Three quick ways to make cost visible:"
  1) Per-route token breakdown (tokens by prompt section)
  2) Synthetic 'monthly at N TPS' costing visualization (low/med/high)
  3) Batching + KV impact projection (tokens saved / % latency change)

Sample numbers (placeholders to swap with real data in run):
- Median request length: 120 tokens
- 95th latency (no cache): 420ms
- 95th latency (with cache + batching): 160ms
- Baseline cost per 1k tokens: $3.40 -> optimized $1.90 (example)

Open questions for product/ML before final deck:
- What two curated model variants should we recommend as primary+fallback for mid-market pilots? (action: Priya to propose list by 2025-06-20).
- Can we provide a canned metrics dashboard template in Console for pilots? (action: Ethan).

Notes-to-self / rough cut copy for slide art direction:
- Keep visuals minimal. Use three color bands: reliability, cost, control.
- Use a micro-chart comparing 'perceived-latency' (user-facing) vs measured token-latency to connect engineering and PM concerns.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- pilot checklist ticket: JIRA-4821
- example tracing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/137
- Slack thread for pilot coordination: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p167890

Unresolved / stretch ideas (future iterations):
- Small interactive slide that runs a live cost calc when you paste median request size. Could ship as a tiny JS widget in Console.
- Packaged canary automation runbook that auto-executes the 2-week A/B and produces the three exit metrics.

End — this is intentionally a sketch. Need SEs to try in 3 pilots, collect data, then iterate into a polished 6-slide flipdeck + 1-pager for legal/procurement.
